segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹכֵר יֵינוֹ לְנׇכְרִי, פָּסַק עַד שֶׁלֹּא מָדַד — דָּמָיו מוּתָּרִין, מָדַד עַד שֶׁלֹּא פָּסַק — דָּמָיו אֲסוּרִין.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of a Jew «who sells his wine to a gentile,» if «he fixed» a price «before he measured» the wine into the gentile’s vessel, deriving benefit from «the money» paid «for» the wine is «permitted.» It is not tantamount to selling wine used for a libation, as the gentile purchased the wine before it became forbidden, and the money already belonged to the Jew. But if the Jew «measured» the wine into the gentile’s vessel, thereby rendering it forbidden, «before he fixed» a price, «the money» paid «for» the wine is «forbidden.»

moves.summary: fixing the price vs measuring first

positions.claim: price fixed before measuring — money permitted; measured before fixing — money forbidden
